verdict.rationale: Activepieces' flow docs say flow actions can include "running code", so a code step inside a workflow is a first-party capability. That is the only mention: the evidence doesn't say which languages are supported, how the step works, or what it can access. Building custom pieces in TypeScript is a separate piece-development capability and earns no credit here. Missing for 10: confirmation of JavaScript and/or Python support, dedicated code-step documentation (inputs/outputs, packages, runtime limits), and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drop into real code (JavaScript or Python) as a step inside a workflow

citations.quote: Actions come after the trigger and control what occurs when the flow is activated, like running code or communicating with other services.
